newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Highlights of 1995 deal on Hebron pullout.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of 1995 deal on Hebron pullout.

text.p: Israel and the PLO remain deeply divided over Israeli army redeployment in Hebron, more than a year after the Jewish state agreed to hand over most of the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule.
Israel's new right-wing government wants to modify the agreement it inherited from the previous administration, while Palestinians refuse to renegotiate any part of the accord.
Following are highlights of Article Seven of the self-rule deal signed in Washington on September 28, 1995 dealing with Hebron:

-- Israel will redeploy its troops in Hebron except for places and roads where arrangements are necessary for the security and protection of Israelis and their movement. An attached map shows the boundaries of area H1 which will be handed over to the PLO and H2 which will remain under Israeli security control.
-- Israeli army redeployment will be completed no later than six months after the signing of the agreement. (Israeli army redeployment was due to have been completed on March 28.)
-- Up to 400 Palestinian policemen, equipped with 20 vehicles and armed with 200 pistols and 100 rifles will take charge of security in area H1.

-- Israel will remain in charge of security in area H2, where about 400 Jewish settlers live among thousands of Palestinians. Joint mobile units will operate throughout the city, including the Old City (which is part of Israeli- controlled H2). Israel will maintain overall security for Israelis in both parts of town.

-- Israel will hand over civil powers and responsibilities in all of the town to the Hebron municipality except for those relating to Israelis and their property. The Hebron municipality will provide services to both sides of the city and will deploy unarmed plainclothes inspectors to monitor and enforce vis-a-vis Palestinians laws and regulations.

-- Israel will implement confidence-building measures, including the Topening produce market in the Old City of Hebron, removing Israeli military roadblocks and the reopening of main entrance of Hebron university.
